notes.title: Monthly Development Update - July 2025
notes.content:
[p]This month has been all about momentum. Planets, missions, and the systems that tie it all together. Our third Planet (official name incoming) is well underway, with fresh terrain, environmental effects, and some seriously mind-bending rocks and trees. Facility design is expanding fast, and our mission system is starting to feel fully alive..[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/08654957339491d71802b7ee76f1a20396a5e5df.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Players will notice smoother targeting, better feedback, new HUD elements, and dynamic music shifts that respond to gameplay. We’ve also implemented mission loading screens, real-time death drops, and refined how Facilities rotate on the Mission Map.
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/61b1e0e0d5678bf2ee7f07811a029205e9d09ec5.jpg"][/img][/p][p]
Meanwhile, behind the scenes, we’ve been optimizing just about everything, from material meshes to how Facility maps stream in and out. Beamable now manages all mission and planet state data.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/d8b71491f567b46a7ea049e2b020b5e1e2f27e18.jpg"][/img][/p][p]And of course, with [url="https://www.gamescom.global/en"]gamescom[/url] 2025 on the horizon, we’ve been laying the groundwork for a big showing, tightening our GTM plan, while we prepare for our closed Beta launch.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/7b36e33f805925b97ef06c687fb36cd0c93f96fd.jpg"][/img][/p][h3]Let’s get into it.[/h3]

notes.title: Monthly Development Update - May 2025
notes.content:
We covered all fronts this month at Warped Games, from game dev to marketing to backend infrastructure. One of the biggest wins was the momentum we’ve seen on our Steam page. We’ve spent the past six months consistently updating it with new content, visuals, and community posts. That kind of work doesn’t pay off immediately, it takes time, iteration, and a lot of convincing to get people to hit that Wishlist button. But this month, it clicked.

Thanks to a strong marketing push, more eyes are landing on Warped Universe, and more people are deciding it’s worth a spot on their wishlist. What’s even more exciting is that those numbers are now growing organically, players are discovering the game through other Steam pages, features, and community recommendations. That’s hugely rewarding, and we’ll keep building on that visibility with regular updates and gameplay reveals.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/0fc41f40221a09f57c92fc20a4c0879b3aa3bca1.png[/img]
This month we focused heavily on ships, both player and Void. Void ships used to be simple palette-swapped versions of player ships. That’s now completely changed. Our art and design teams worked together to create an entirely new aesthetic for the Void, pulling more from their origin in the lore and pushing them into something far more eerie and distinct. The new models look truly warped and hostile, exactly as they should!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/9dfa4309393c8103a9dbb93468d6c002b363b0e4.jpg[/img]
Player ships got a major upgrade too. We added loads of new cosmetic parts (like sails, tails, tusks, wings, hulls, masks, and auras), and reworked ship materials across all five battlepass tiers. These changes give players much more control over their visual identity in the universe. We also introduced new aura FX and a modular base system for internal ship skeletons to support even more variations in the future.

A lot of time this month went into tightening gameplay systems and combat feedback. Ammo was removed from player weapons to streamline combat, and damage numbers have been added for both player and enemy hits. This alone makes encounters feel more readable and reactive.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/adf4c006f9b7ee20299a36d495bc6a999430a96a.png[/img]
On the backend side, we synced our latest work with Beamable and continued expanding tools and systems for development. Niagara FX scripts and emitters were pushed to handle new skeletal effects, and we laid the groundwork for future mission interactions by building a flexible base to build them on top of.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/8cdc2c173da17d46d3ed071f7cba6ce3c2e2394c.png[/img]
That’s it for this month’s game development update. We’re making Warped Universe deeper, sharper, and more reactive across the board. Thanks for continuing to follow the journey, whether you're here for the lore, the systems, or just to watch the ships explode in style, we’re glad you’re along for the ride.

[b]Wishlist us on Steam if you haven’t already, and let us know what you think in the comments or on Discord![/b]

notes.title: The Living Map of the Warped Universe
notes.content:
[i]"The System Status Map is a direct projection of the state of our sprawling and fragile environment. As the frontier’s pylons are built and stabilized, sector matter and energy is directly reflected in real time here in the center of Nexus Station. Part model, part news broadcast, part mission board. It's the focus of every warp pioneer, these warped particles entangled at a tiny ratio with the chaos out there. It's the pulse - the vital signs of the star system, and thus we must all monitor it closely."[/i]
[b]- Dr Monica Monos[/b]

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

While many parts of Nexus Station help prepare a player for their journey, one in particular shows them where their actions truly matter. That’s the System Status Map, a massive interactive map of the known universe, displaying live data, and real-time player influence.
At the heart of the monitor is the system’s sun. More than just a visual set piece, the star reflects the Balance of Light and Gravity, a global system mechanic that shifts based on collective player behavior. Each mission you complete tips the scales in one direction or the other.
As the balance shifts further in either direction, certain changes in gameplay occur, movement speed, resistances, damage and skills are all affected

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/3bfd9b3f018576f929790d3481657cc793e330ed.jpg[/img]
Every visual marker is interactive, offering mission options, cooperative goals, and strategic alerts. Whether you're soloing a scout mission or teaming up to contain a Void outbreak, your actions feed into this living display, and the monitor updates in real time..

The System Map shows not just where you can go, but why it matters. Players can see:
[list]
[*] Planets - Both completed and in construction
[*] Facilities on planets - Showing how developed or vulnerable they are
[*] Unmapped sectors - Explore mission areas obscured by Void interference
[*] Active void tears - Unstable zones where enemy invasions are occurring
[*] Pylon networks - Vital objectives required to stabilize new regions and expand the system
[*] Residuum Deposits - Collection and Transport missions required to facilitate the construction of Planets
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/9a3d170d37f1d8d8811e5066d69cf14eadc7f8b4.jpg[/img]
Each facility type adds significant benefits and opportunities upon completion that remain as long as the facility is operational. 

Facility upgrades include:
[list]
[*] Farm Facilities - Provide a health bonus to players embarking on missions
[*] Housing Facilities - Adds choice and reduces costs of end of mission rewards
[*] Power Facilities - Increases the rarity of mission rewards
[*] Factory Facilities - Adds the possibility of rolling certain attributes on equipment obtained from Artifractal Cores
[*] Research Facilities - Increase the Potential of any new piece of equipment in that category 
[*] Spaceport Facilities - Required to kick start a new planet once discovered and constructed
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/0c81f5bacdafac2774bdae36918118d0d58871e5.jpg[/img]
Each of these upgrades is improved further as more of each type of facility is completed throughout the system, changing gameplay options significantly from start of season to the end. 

There’s a strange sensation when using the System Monitor: you feel like a miniature piece on a galactic game board. And in some sense, you are. But unlike a traditional game, the board is unfinished, unmapped, and at risk.
This is what makes the SSM feel alive: it doesn't just reflect the state of the game, it is the state of the game.

The System Status Map turns abstract player behavior into visible consequence. It tracks a shared universe, responds to individual decisions, and serves as the connective tissue for strategy, cooperation, and survival.

It’s not just where you get missions. It’s where you see your impact. Every new region you open, every planet that forms, every moment of collapse or recovery... it all echoes on this surface.

notes.title: The Constant Conflict
notes.content:
[i]"The endless challenges of propagating a secure population include the construction and maintenance of strange, technically wondrous feats of engineering while beset by a ceaseless tide of invasion. After a time, one yearns for the drudgery of monotonous tasks when the spectre of destruction lurks around every corner. But just as we strive for balance in the universal forces, we must also balance our efforts between the impressive and the inane. The perils are seemingly insurmountable, but the rewards defy imagination. We do what we do not only for the bounty of victory, but also because it is the right thing to do."[/i]
[b]- Orin[/b]

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

At its core, Warped Universe is a battle for creation and survival faced with the constant threat of annihilation. The remnants of a shattered civilization drift over silent distances, caught between the fluctuating forces of Light and Gravity. Players travel to the ruins of this universe, re-shaping its fate through strategic exploration, planetary construction, and high intensity battles.
Missions run the full gamut between complex infiltrations of construction areas on the untamed frontier to simple data collection goals in sparsely infested farmlands. Regardless of the setting and threat, each excursion into the young system’s environments brings a variety of challenges and strategies. Players can always choose a threat level and pace that appeals to their gaming senses.
Our conflict extends beyond simple good versus evil. It’s a struggle of balance, where every action shifts the cosmic scales. Whether you embrace the speed and precision of Light or the raw control and power of Gravity, your choices will influence the battlefield and the universe itself.
Shifting Balance

In Warped Universe the choices players make, and the missions they take have an ever changing effect on the state of the seasons system and gameplay. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/0bbeac853a87ece348b0440c5543f48c71c6ae39.jpg[/img]
The star in the center of the map will show the current balance of Gravity and Light, the effects of which include changing movement speed, jump distance, how skills function, damage, resistances, and more. In the most extreme cases of imbalance, Void enemies will even receive a hefty damage buff. It’ll be up to players to decide whether they want to keep the balance or push it to one side or the other. You may want high gravity to take advantage of a certain loadout and skills, while others may prefer light or to pull things back to the center. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/f7f2413e08c551bf00dc26cbfdaf11c0e31ba570.jpg[/img]
The way in which players direct the balance will come in the form of completing missions assigned to either the Luminaries or Foundationalists. Farms, Housing, and Factory missions push balance towards gravity, while Power, Research, and Space Port missions lean towards the Light. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/04e11fbfa8e1f8e75a667385acfe3390f17b0e35.jpg[/img]
These of course aren't the only mission types you’ll find on the System Map. There are also Explore missions, which are needed to open up the map to find new potential resources. In Pylon missions, players build and defend a network of pylons responsible for creating a safe zone required to begin mining resources or to build a new planet. Residuum missions are escort missions retrieving and transporting Residuum back to Nexus Station. Finally there are the Void Tear missions. Void Tears are a constant threat in the Warped Universe. If a Void Tear isn't closed in time, it can destroy a facility and set back all of the progress made by players. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/f395f9d50f7f0f1e831dde46533ae248fb241c59.jpg[/img]
It will be up to you and the other inhabitants of Warped Universe to decide how much gets explored, which facilities are built, and what is saved. 
[h3]
The Choice is Yours.[/h3]

notes.title: Join us for our monthly town hall on Discord
notes.content:
Dear Warped Community, 

It’s that time of the month again – Warped Talk + Live Q&A kicks off Thursday, April 3rd at 9 PM UTC 

Following our exciting trip to the Sui Gaming Summit at GDC in San Francisco, where we presented the Warped Universe to the public for the very first time, we’re going live on Discord and across YouTube, and X to show you what you missed – and what’s coming next.

This is a huge milestone for Warped Universe. We’ve been grinding for many months to bring this moment to life, and we couldn’t be more thrilled to share it with you. 

That’s why tomorrow’s Warped Talk isn’t one to be missed as we’ll be:  
[list]
[*] Showing new gameplay (and more) 
[*] Recapping our experience at Sui Gaming Summit 
[*] Talking through current updates and progress
[*] Answering all your questions! 
[/list]
[h3]Join the Warped Games Discord here:[/h3]
https://discord.gg/warpedgames


From founding Warped back in 2023 to working relentlessly throughout 2025 bringing our vision to life, to now presenting Warped Universe at events across the world - none of this would be possible without the support of our community. 

Thank you for being part of this journey, now it’s time to get excited for the year ahead. 

Stay Warped.

notes.title: Space At Your Pace
notes.content:
[i][h3]Not only is matter and energy altered in the warped universe, one’s perception of chronicity can be commanded in unexpected ways. Unfettered by the biological limitations of synaptic impulse potential, a mind can choose to move the echo in a more natural way, or process inputs in a state which may feel that time itself is standing still.[/h3][/i]

Drawing from our passion for diverse gaming experiences, we have developed an innovative design that integrates multiple genres within a single environment. This allows players to select their mission and then choose their preferred gameplay style, whether real-time action or turn-based strategy. Both genres utilize the same weapons, skills, damage systems, and mechanics, creating a fluid transition that enhances immersion, increases engagement, and broadens appeal.

[h3]Real-Time Action[/h3]
As a third-person action shooter, both as a character on the ground, or a ship up in space, this gameplay style caters to fast-paced thrill-seekers.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/3a8f18e686f71ebb2168028c63e6489f0ef2cc62.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/c92a9941f4a140c46726ca3fe3e5ddff3a655d94.jpg[/img]

[h3]Turn-Based Strategy[/h3]
This top-down game style is ideal for players who prefer a more tactical approach. Utilizing action points and dice rolls to determine the outcomes of your missions. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/1f1397e066945ed3c0752efb6ffbad56aefea43f.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/ab09972be0dfffc05bb28b3d4a421f06be87a817.jpg[/img]
[h3]Play Your Way[/h3]
By allowing players to select how they engage with each mission, Warped Universe caters to a wide range of playstyles while encouraging collaboration across the community. This innovative approach draws on the preferred mechanics of popular real-time games like Fortnite and Helldivers 2, as well as successful turn-based strategy mechanics found in Dungeons and Dragons and XCOM, making Warped Universe appeal to an audience with diverse gaming preferences.
